newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak actors to strike against state intervention.
newsitem.headline: Slovak actors to strike against state intervention.

text.p: The actors of Slovakia's prestigious National Theatre on Wednesday stepped up their protest against the government of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar saying they will begin an indefinite strike.

"There will be no public theatre performances as of Thursday," Ladislav Chudik, the internationally-respected doyen of Slovakia's acting community told a rally of some 10,000 people gathered in central Bratislava on Thursday.
Wednesday's rally was held to protest Culture Minister Ivan Hudec's sacking of National Theatre General-Director Dusan Jamrich, who was replaced by Miroslav Fischer, the manager of the Chamber Opera.
"We shall continue to rehearse...but will not perform until proper competition is announced for the post of general-director," Chudik said.

The only other time the National Theatre closed down was in November 1989 when actors in then-Czechoslovakia went on strike and held protest meetings which helpded spark the "Velvet Revolution" which brought down the communist government.
Hudec further angered the country's intellectual community by sacking chief of the Slovak Philharmonic, Karol Faith.
At least 35,000 people have signed a petition protesting against state interference in the autonomy of cultural institutions and called for Hudec to resign.
Artists and intellectuals have always enjoyed high respect in the Czech and Slovak lands and wield greater authority than in many other countries.
They have been outspoken in their criticism of the Meciar government which they say is increasingly authoritarian.
Last month the National Theatre ensemble called on Hudec to resign on grounds of incompetence after he had sacked the theatre's drama artistic director.

The actors said Hudec had violated the autonomy of the theatre by appointing Lubomir Paulovic, a member of the national theatre ensemble, and sacking his predecessor without consulting Jamrich. Paulovic later resigned and quit the national theatre,
There has been growing fear among intellectuals about attempts by the government to undermine and control the artistic and academic communities and sap their independence.

Last week Meciar's ruling majority approved a controversial amendment to higher education laws, giving the Education Ministry the power to cancel decisions of universities on, among other things, the awarding of academic titles.
